description:
About the Position

The University of Exeter offers a fully funded PhD studentship on 2D materials-reinforced multifunctional coatings for built environments. The project develops coatings reinforced with two-dimensional materials to improve durability, functionality and environmental performance of surfaces and structures in the built environment.

The doctoral candidate will synthesise and characterise 2D-material-reinforced coating systems, test mechanical and functional properties, and evaluate performance under realistic built-environment conditions. The studentship provides an annual stipend of GBP 21,805 together with fee coverage, and is based in the university's engineering research environment with access to advanced materials characterisation facilities.

Candidate Profile

Applicants hold (or expect to obtain) a first-class or upper second-class degree, or a master's qualification, in materials science, chemistry, physics, engineering or a related discipline. Experience in materials synthesis or coating technology is an advantage. The studentship is open to UK and international applicants under the published funding rules, and the application deadline is fixed.

Highlights

  • 2D materials for reinforced coatings
  • Multifunctional surface engineering
  • Durability and environmental performance testing
  • Built-environment applications
  • Advanced materials characterisation
  • Fully funded studentship, GBP 21,805 annual stipend
